text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-President Elias Hrawi will nominate Rafik al-Hariri as prime minister today to form a new cabinet after he got the backing of the majority of MPs who were consulted by Hrawi.
-Christian opposition MP Boutros Harb declares his wealth to parliament and urges all the politicians to follow suit.
-The Lebanese army has received French military aid.
-Hariri will meet Syrian President Hafez al-Assad before his nomination for a third term of office.
-Hariri will consult MPs on Saturday and Sunday to form the new cabinet.
-Central bank governor Salameh says: "The public debt is a serious issue and administrative reform is needed in order to keep the debt under control."
-Assad met former prime minister Selim al-Hoss in Damascus.
-Foreign Minister Faris Bouez says French President Jacques Chirac's tour in the Middle East shows a new French dynamic in dealing with problems.
-Two thirds of the old cabinet will be in the new one.
-President Chirac, who arrives in Beirut today, will spend the night at the presidential palace in Baabda.
-Hariri: "We are seeking a European and French role that complements the American role in the Middle East."
-Christian Maronite Patriarch Nasrallah Sfeir: "Lebanon's independence is incomplete, its decision is controlled from abroad and the foreign forces forbid stability."
